original_card.question: Can one of the selected record's five inherited assumptions be proved at its actual caller?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one assumption ID (native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery), one quantified implication and exact dependency closure. Check current handoffs, including #5625 row reentry and #5707 root-prefix lowering, without treating their partial scope as the whole theorem. Prove or falsify that implication with a caller-bound argument; stop at the chosen obligation. Finite tests or root digits do not discharge an all-size statement.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: Open question 2 of research/mode-fiber-radius-bounds (#6320, merged): lower the upper bound R <= 2 on the least uniform l_inf radius R of exact mode-preserving integer rounding for the PR4933 mode map M, posed after #6312's open question 1.
scope_change_reason: Continues the merged #6320 package, which changed this card to #6312's self-contained radius question. That package's second open question had a concrete first step; this package answers it with a different, shorter argument.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the precision contract of the coded inverse. It bounds what an exact mode-preserving rounder can achieve on this M; it does not show that any caller needs one, and changes no kappa.
stop_rule: Stop at a written proof of an upper bound below 2 whose finite inputs are checked exactly, or at an exact counterexample to the balancing lemma. Do not claim R = 1.
evidence: PROOF.md Theorem D (R <= 3/2) with verify.py exact checks: the 14 pinned blocks, H8 closure and complements, column sums divisible by 8, rainbow and straight matchings with their pair identities, the 16-case balancing table, 150 exact rounder runs and seven rejection controls. A separate 12,000-input exact stress run found no failure (worst error 1259/840).

open_questions.question: Is R = 1, that is, is every lattice point of L in the open zonotope int Z a 0/1 subset sum of rows (Theorem A of #6320)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It settles #6312's question exactly; the #6320 search sample supports yes, and 1 <= R <= 3/2 is now known.
open_questions.first_step: Treat rows with |v_i| > 1/4 specially: add the sign constraints sgn v'_i = sgn v_i to the vertex polytope, and use the slack of the balancing lemma (n_j >= 6 against |u_j| <= 4) to fix the rows those constraints leave at 0.
open_questions.blocked_by: Rows that stop at 0 snap with error 1/2 into u, and there is no bound on how many stop there.
